peopleAlsoAsk.question: What is avian paramyxovirus?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Avian Paramyxoviruses (APMV) are a group of RNA viruses that cause acute respiratory or neurologic disease. There are 12 recognized serotypes of avian paramyxoviruses (APMV-1 to APMV-12). In wildlife, avian paramyxovirus is most typically seen in cormorants and gulls.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What particle size requires airborne precautions?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Airborne transmission has been attributed to only a few pathogens, notably Mycobacterium tuberculosis, via infectious droplet nuclei that are particles sized 5 μm or smaller. The use of airborne infection isolation rooms and respirator masks has been recommended only to protect against airborne transmission.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What is avian paramyxovirus type 1 apmv 1 virus?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Avian paramyxovirus serotype-1 (APMV-1) is a member of the Paramyxoviridae family and is the causative agent of virulent Newcastle disease (vND). The virus is able to infect all orders of avian species, and virulent strains can cause significant clinical signs.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What type of virus is paramyxovirus?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: The Paramyxoviridae is a family of single-stranded RNA viruses known to cause different types of infections in vertebrates. Examples of these infections in humans include the measles virus, mumps virus, parainfluenza virus, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
